concepts.name: The basic economic problem: scarcity, choice and the three questions
concepts.description: Needs and wants, finite resources and unlimited wants, scarcity and the need to choose, examples of the basic economic problem for consumers, workers, firms and governments, economic goods versus free goods, and the three questions of what, how and for whom to produce. Opportunity cost is separate; how each economic system answers the questions is in econ.systems.types.

concepts.name: Opportunity cost
concepts.description: Definition of opportunity cost as the next best alternative forgone, examples in different contexts, and how opportunity cost influences the decisions of consumers, workers, firms and governments. Opportunity cost on a PPC is in econ.basics.ppc.

concepts.name: Production possibility curves: points and movements
concepts.description: Definition and construction of a PPC from a table of output combinations, points on, inside and outside the curve (efficient, inefficient, unattainable), movements along the curve and the opportunity cost they show, and efficient resource allocation. Shapes and shifts are in econ.basics.ppc-shapes-shifts.

concepts.name: PPC shapes and shifts
concepts.description: Concave (bowed out), straight-line and convex PPCs and what each shape says about opportunity cost (shapes are ZIMSEC depth); outward and inward shifts of a PPC, their causes (changes in the quantity and quality of resources, technology, disasters, emigration) and consequences for economic growth.

concepts.name: Positive and normative statements
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Statements of fact that can be tested (positive) versus value judgements and opinions (normative), recognising each in economic discussion.

concepts.name: Factors of production and their rewards
concepts.description: Land, labour, capital and enterprise defined with examples; their rewards (rent, wages or salaries, interest, profit or loss); causes of changes in the quantity and quality of each factor (for example education and training, investment, migration, discovery of resources, land degradation).

concepts.name: Economic systems: market, planned and mixed
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Cambridge defines the market and mixed systems in the next two concepts). Features of market (free enterprise), planned (command) and mixed economies, who owns resources and makes decisions in each, and how each system answers what, how and for whom to produce. Arguments for and against are in the next two concepts.

concepts.name: The market economic system
concepts.description: Definition of the market economic system (private ownership, decisions through markets, limited government), its advantages (choice, efficiency, incentives, innovation) and disadvantages (inequality, market failure, under-provision of public and merit goods, instability).

concepts.name: Markets and the price mechanism
concepts.description: Definition and examples of a market (including informal markets), the roles of buyers and sellers, and how the price mechanism (signalling, incentive and rationing functions) allocates resources and answers what, how and for whom to produce.

concepts.name: Planned and mixed economies
concepts.description: Advantages and disadvantages of planned and mixed economies; definition of a mixed economy and arguments for and against it; comparing the three systems; Zimbabwe's current economic system as a mixed economy (roles of the state, parastatals, private firms and the informal sector, described without statistics).

concepts.name: Demand and the law of demand
concepts.description: Definition of demand, effective demand versus latent (potential) demand, the law of demand, demand schedules and curves, and individual versus market demand (adding individual schedules). Shifts are in econ.demand.shifts.

concepts.name: Changes in demand and changes in quantity demanded
concepts.description: Determinants of demand other than price (income, prices of substitutes and complements, tastes, population, advertising, expectations, taxes), extensions and contractions along a demand curve versus increases and decreases that shift it, described in words and with schedules.

concepts.name: Supply and the law of supply
concepts.description: Definition of supply, the law of supply, supply schedules and curves, and individual versus market supply. Shifts are in econ.supply.shifts.

concepts.name: Changes in supply and changes in quantity supplied
concepts.description: Determinants of supply other than price (costs of production, technology, weather, prices of related goods, number of firms, taxes and subsidies, expectations), extensions and contractions versus increases and decreases in supply.

concepts.name: Climate change and production
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. What climate change is, its effects on production in Zimbabwe (drought, floods, crop yields, livestock, hydro-electricity) and measures to mitigate and adapt (conservation farming, drought-resistant crops, irrigation, reforestation, renewable energy). Well-established facts only.

concepts.name: Market equilibrium and disequilibrium
concepts.description: Equilibrium price and quantity from demand and supply schedules and curves, disequilibrium prices, shortages (excess demand) and surpluses (excess supply), and how the market moves back to equilibrium.

concepts.name: Price changes: shifts and new equilibrium
concepts.description: How changes in demand and supply cause price changes, finding the new equilibrium after a shift (described in words and with schedules), and the consequences of price changes for sales.

concepts.name: Maximum and minimum prices
concepts.description: Government price ceilings (maximum prices) and price floors (minimum prices) in product markets: definitions, effects shown with schedules and described diagrams (shortages, queues, black markets, surpluses), advantages and disadvantages. Minimum wages are in econ.labour.unions-government.

concepts.name: Indirect taxes and subsidies in product markets
concepts.description: How an indirect tax (specific and ad valorem) shifts supply and raises price, how a subsidy lowers price, the effects on consumers, producers and government, and their advantages and disadvantages as ways to correct market failure.

concepts.name: Regulation, privatisation, nationalisation and direct provision
concepts.description: Definitions, advantages and disadvantages of regulation, privatisation, nationalisation, direct provision of goods and services, and quotas (for example on extracting natural resources) as responses to market failure.

concepts.name: Price elasticity of demand: calculation and values
concepts.description: Definition of PED, the formula (percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price), calculating it, interpreting values (perfectly inelastic, inelastic, unitary, elastic, perfectly elastic) and describing the demand curve for each.

concepts.name: Determinants of price elasticity of demand
concepts.description: Main influences on PED: availability of substitutes, proportion of income spent, necessity or luxury, habit and addiction, time, definition of the market.

concepts.name: PED, spending and revenue
concepts.description: How price changes affect consumer spending and firms' total revenue depending on PED (shown by calculation and described diagrams), and the significance of PED for households, firms, workers and government (pricing, taxation).

concepts.name: Income and cross elasticity of demand
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Formulas, calculation and interpretation of income elasticity (normal, inferior, luxury goods) and cross elasticity (substitutes, complements, unrelated goods), and their importance to firms and government.

concepts.name: Price elasticity of supply
concepts.description: Definition, formula and calculation of PES, interpreting values (perfectly inelastic to perfectly elastic) and the supply curve for each, determinants (time, spare capacity, stocks, ease of switching factors, nature of the product) and its importance in real situations such as farming.

concepts.name: Market failure: public, merit and demerit goods
concepts.description: Definition of market failure; public goods (non-rival, non-excludable, free-rider problem) and their non-provision by markets; merit goods and under-consumption; demerit goods and over-consumption. Abuse of monopoly power is in econ.structures.monopoly.

concepts.name: Private, external and social costs and benefits
concepts.description: Private costs and benefits, external costs and benefits (externalities), social cost = private cost + external cost and social benefit = private benefit + external benefit, with calculations, and the over-production of goods with external costs and under-production of goods with external benefits. No market-failure diagrams.

concepts.name: Barter and money: forms, functions and characteristics
concepts.description: Barter and its problems (double coincidence of wants), forms and types of money (commodity, coins, notes, bank deposits, electronic and mobile money), money supply measures M1, M2 and M3 (ZIMSEC), functions of money and the characteristics of good money.

concepts.name: Commercial banks, other financial institutions and the central bank
concepts.description: Role and importance of commercial banks (deposits, loans, payments, credit creation in outline), merchant banks and building societies; role and importance of a central bank (issuing currency, banker to the government and to banks, lender of last resort, monetary policy, exchange-rate management, supervision), with the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe as the local example.

concepts.name: Households: spending, saving and borrowing
concepts.description: Cambridge only. How income, the rate of interest, confidence, age and culture influence households' spending, saving and borrowing.

concepts.name: Workers: types of workers and choosing an occupation
concepts.description: Labour and its reward, unskilled, semi-skilled and skilled workers, employees' interests (wages, security, health and safety, fringe benefits), and the wage and non-wage factors that affect an individual's choice of occupation.

concepts.name: Trade unions, employers and government in wage setting
concepts.description: Employers' associations, trade unions and workers' committees and their roles; collective bargaining and relative bargaining power; government intervention in wage determination, including a national minimum wage and its effects on the labour market (described with schedules).

concepts.name: Demand for and supply of labour; wage determination
concepts.description: Derived demand for labour, factors affecting the demand for and supply of labour, the equilibrium wage in a labour market and the effects of changes in demand or supply, described in words and with schedules.

concepts.name: Wage differentials
concepts.description: Why wages differ: demand and supply of labour, skills and training, risk, prestige, bargaining strength, discrimination (for example by gender), government policy, culture; differences by skill, by sector (primary, secondary, tertiary) and between private and public sectors.

concepts.name: Mobility of labour
concepts.description: Occupational and geographical mobility of labour, causes of changes in each (skills, training, housing costs, family ties, information) and their consequences for workers, firms and the economy.

concepts.name: Specialisation and division of labour
concepts.description: Definition of division of labour (worker specialisation) and specialisation, with examples at home, school and in industry, and its advantages and disadvantages.

concepts.name: Stages of production and value addition
concepts.description: Primary, secondary and tertiary production (sectors) with examples, how they depend on each other, value addition and why it matters to Zimbabwe (for example processing minerals and farm produce), and direct versus indirect production.

concepts.name: Zimbabwe's land reform
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The aims of Zimbabwe's land reform programme and its economic effects (positive and negative) on agricultural production, employment and the economy, using only well-established facts and balanced views; no disputed statistics.

concepts.name: Production and productivity
concepts.description: The difference between production and productivity, measuring productivity (output per worker or per hour), total, average and marginal product (ZIMSEC), influences on productivity, ways of improving it and the effect of investment on productivity.

concepts.name: Demand for factors; labour-intensive and capital-intensive production
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Influences on firms' demand for factors of production (demand for the product, factor prices, availability, productivity) and reasons for, advantages and disadvantages of labour-intensive and capital-intensive production.

concepts.name: Location of industry
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Factors affecting where firms locate (raw materials, markets, labour, power, transport, water, government policy) and how and why government influences location (incentives, restrictions, infrastructure, growth points).

concepts.name: Costs of production
concepts.description: Fixed, variable, semi-variable and total costs; average fixed, average variable and average total cost; calculating them from a table; how costs change with output (described curves); short run versus long run.

concepts.name: Revenue
concepts.description: Total revenue and average revenue (and marginal revenue for ZIMSEC): definitions, calculations from price and quantity tables, and how sales affect revenue.

concepts.name: Marginal analysis, profit and efficiency
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Marginal cost and marginal revenue, the profit-maximising rule MR = MC, normal and abnormal (supernormal) profit and losses, break-even where AR = AC, and allocative and productive efficiency.

concepts.name: Objectives of firms
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Survival, social welfare, profit maximisation and growth as objectives, and why objectives differ between firms and over time.

concepts.name: Forms of business organisation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Features, advantages and disadvantages of sole traders, partnerships, co-operatives and private and public limited companies, comparing them, and the documents for forming a company (memorandum and articles of association, certificate of incorporation, trading certificate) and what they contain.

concepts.name: Private and public sector firms; public corporations
concepts.description: Private-sector versus public-sector firms, public corporations (parastatals) and their features, advantages and disadvantages.

concepts.name: Small and large firms; growth and mergers
concepts.description: Advantages and disadvantages of small and large firms, internal and external growth, horizontal, vertical and conglomerate mergers (integration): definitions, examples, advantages, disadvantages and effects on stakeholders.

concepts.name: Economies and diseconomies of scale
concepts.description: Internal economies (technical, purchasing, marketing, financial, risk-bearing, managerial) and external economies, internal and external diseconomies, and the long-run average total cost curve described in words and tables.

concepts.name: Multinational companies
concepts.description: Features of multinational companies (MNCs) and their advantages and disadvantages to host countries and home countries.

concepts.name: Sources of finance for firms
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Methods of raising capital: shares, debentures, loans, overdrafts, leasing, hire purchase, retained profits, grants; choosing between them.

concepts.name: Small and medium enterprises and business plans
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Features of SMEs, their importance and problems in Zimbabwe, ways SMEs survive, the parts of a business plan and a simple cash-flow projection (with checked arithmetic).

concepts.name: Competitive markets and perfect competition
concepts.description: Characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of competitive markets and the effect of many firms on price, quality, choice and profit (both boards); the features of perfect competition (ZIMSEC). No diagrams for Cambridge.

concepts.name: Monopoly
concepts.description: Characteristics of monopoly, barriers to entry, advantages and disadvantages, the effect of one firm on price, quality, choice and profit, and monopoly as a cause of market failure (restricted supply and higher prices).

concepts.name: Monopolistic competition and oligopoly
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Features, advantages and disadvantages of monopolistic competition, with an outline of oligopoly (few large firms, interdependence, non-price competition).

concepts.name: Price and output in different market structures
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Short-run and long-run equilibrium of the firm in perfect competition, monopolistic competition and monopoly (normal profit, abnormal profit, losses), price and output determination using MR = MC and AR = AC described with tables, and comparing the structures.

concepts.name: National income: GDP, GNP and measurement
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Meaning of GDP and GNP (net income from abroad), the income, output and expenditure methods, the components consumption, investment, government spending, exports and imports, and simple calculations.

concepts.name: Uses and limitations of national income statistics
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. How households, firms, government and international bodies use national income statistics (economic activity and growth, living standards, planning), and limitations: double counting, the informal sector, unrecorded activities, inaccurate data, price changes.

concepts.name: Government macroeconomic aims and conflicts
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Economic growth, full employment, stable prices, balance of payments stability, redistribution of income and environmental sustainability; why governments choose them and set targets; conflicts between aims.

concepts.name: The government budget and fiscal policy
concepts.description: Government budget, deficit and surplus (with calculations), main areas of government spending and their effects, definition of fiscal policy, changes in taxes and spending, and how fiscal policy can help achieve macroeconomic aims (for example closing a deficit or controlling inflation).

concepts.name: Taxation
concepts.description: Reasons for taxation, direct and indirect taxes, progressive, regressive and proportional taxes (with calculations of tax paid and average rates), and the impact of taxation on consumers, workers, firms, the government and the economy.

concepts.name: Monetary policy
concepts.description: Definitions of money supply and monetary policy; changes in interest rates, the money supply and the exchange rate; how monetary policy can help achieve macroeconomic aims, including curbing inflation; the central bank's role.

concepts.name: Supply-side policy
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Definition and measures (education and training, infrastructure spending, labour market reforms, lower direct taxes, deregulation, incentives to work and invest, privatisation) and their effects on macroeconomic aims.

concepts.name: Economic growth: meaning, measurement, causes and consequences
concepts.description: Meaning of economic growth, measurement by real GDP (nominal versus real), signs of growth, causes (increases in total demand and in the quantity and quality of resources), and its advantages and disadvantages (costs and benefits).

concepts.name: Recession and policies to promote growth
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Definition of recession, its causes (falls in total demand or in the quantity or quality of resources) and consequences for consumers, workers, firms and government, and the range of policies to promote growth and their effectiveness.

concepts.name: Economic development and its indicators
concepts.description: Meaning of economic development and how it differs from growth, signs of development (literacy, lower death rates, infrastructure), causes of development, indicators including real GDP per head and the Human Development Index and the advantages and disadvantages of each.

concepts.name: Living standards and international differences in development
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Reasons for differences in living standards and income distribution within and between countries, and how income, productivity, population growth, the size of sectors, saving and investment, education, healthcare and natural resources cause differences in development.

concepts.name: Poverty
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Absolute and relative poverty, causes (unemployment, low wages, illness, age, environmental factors) and policies to alleviate poverty and redistribute income.

concepts.name: Sustainable development and resource management
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Sustainable resource allocation and management (CAMPFIRE, the Environmental Management Agency, community share ownership trusts, recycling), sustainable development, initiatives and projects with their costs and benefits, and lessons from a newly industrialised country.

concepts.name: Inflation: meaning, types and causes
concepts.description: Definitions of inflation and deflation, demand-pull and cost-push inflation and how to distinguish them (other causes such as excessive money creation in outline).

concepts.name: Measuring inflation: price indices
concepts.description: Consumer Price Index (and the Retail Price Index for ZIMSEC): base year, basket, weights, calculating a weighted index and the rate of inflation, comparing rates for different periods. Zimbabwean inflation history only with widely documented, dated facts.

concepts.name: Effects of inflation and policies to control it
concepts.description: How inflation affects consumers, workers, savers, lenders, borrowers, producers, government and the economy, and the functions of money (especially store of value) during high inflation; monetary, fiscal and supply-side policies to control inflation and their effectiveness.

concepts.name: Population size, growth and distribution
concepts.description: Population and the census and why it is conducted; birth rate, death rate, natural increase, immigration, emigration and net migration; factors affecting population growth and why rates differ between countries; geographical, occupational and age-sex distribution of population.

concepts.name: Effects of population size and structure
concepts.description: Optimum, over- and under-population, effects of increases and decreases in population size and of changes in age and gender structure, the dependency ratio, and the link between population and economic development.

concepts.name: HIV and AIDS and the economy
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Causes of the spread of HIV, its effects on population, the labour force and economic development, and solutions; factual, respectful and non-stigmatising.

concepts.name: Size and composition of the labour force
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The economically active population (ages as the syllabus gives them), how the composition of the population relates to the labour force, factors affecting its size and composition (skills, training, government policy) and ways of controlling population growth.

concepts.name: Employment, unemployment and their measurement
concepts.description: Definitions of employment, unemployment, the labour force and full employment; distinguishing the employed from the unemployed; measuring unemployment with a labour force survey and calculating the unemployment rate.

concepts.name: Types and causes of unemployment
concepts.description: Frictional, structural, cyclical and seasonal unemployment (both boards) and regional and technological unemployment (ZIMSEC), with causes and examples.

concepts.name: Effects of unemployment and policies to reduce it
concepts.description: Consequences of unemployment for individuals, firms, government and the economy, and the range of policies to reduce it and their effectiveness.

concepts.name: Unemployment and job creation in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. General unemployment trends in Zimbabwe and the informal sector (no specific statistics unless widely documented and dated), job creation through enterprise and indigenisation, and planning a small income-generating project.

concepts.name: Domestic trade
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Characteristics and importance of domestic (home) trade, retailers and wholesalers, formal and informal trade, and the role of informal traders in Zimbabwe's economy.

concepts.name: Home and foreign trade; specialisation by country
concepts.description: Characteristics of home and foreign trade compared, exports and imports, definition of specialisation by country, and the advantages and disadvantages of international trade and specialisation.

concepts.name: Absolute and comparative advantage
concepts.description: Reasons countries trade: factor endowment, absolute advantage and comparative advantage (with simple output tables and opportunity cost ratios), and specialisation based on the best resource allocation or lowest cost.

concepts.name: Free trade
concepts.description: Definition of free trade, its advantages and disadvantages.

concepts.name: Protectionism
concepts.description: Methods of protection (tariffs, import quotas, subsidies, embargoes, exchange controls), reasons (infant and declining industries, strategic industries, dumping, the current account deficit, tax revenue, demerit goods, the environment), and the consequences, advantages and disadvantages of restricting trade.

concepts.name: Globalisation
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Definition, causes of changes in globalisation (trade restrictions, transport and communication costs, movement of MNCs) and its effects on trade, competition, the environment, migration, income distribution and development.

concepts.name: Economic integration: SADC, COMESA and the African Union
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Forms and reasons for economic integration, the aims of SADC, COMESA and the African Union (well-established facts only), and the benefits and problems of integration for Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Terms of trade
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Terms of trade = index of export prices ÷ index of import prices × 100, calculating it, favourable and unfavourable movements and what they mean.

concepts.name: Foreign exchange rates
concepts.description: Definition, reasons for buying and selling currencies, floating exchange rates determined by demand and supply, appreciation and depreciation, causes of fluctuations (trade, interest rates, speculation), and effects of changes on the prices of and demand for exports and imports, with simple conversions.

concepts.name: Foreign currency shortages
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Causes and problems of foreign exchange shortages and the possible sources of foreign currency for Zimbabwe (exports of minerals and farm produce, tourism, remittances, investment, loans), described without disputed statistics.

concepts.name: The balance of trade and the current account
concepts.description: Visible and invisible trade, the balance of trade, the components of the current account (trade in goods, trade in services, primary income, secondary income), calculating balances and interpreting deficits and surpluses.

concepts.name: Current account deficits and surpluses: causes, consequences and policies
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Reasons for current account deficits and surpluses, their impact on GDP, employment, inflation and the exchange rate, and policies to achieve balance of payments stability.
